chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When the woman says to her husband in a general statement: 'I will not obey you in any matter, specified or unspecified,' it becomes permissible for him to take from her (her dowry/mahr) without having to return it to her.

key_terms.رَجَعَةٌ: Return (specifically of the dowry in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband keeping his wife's dowry if she generally declares disobedience?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-istibsar clarifies the legal mechanism of *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife), establishing that a general declaration of disobedience grants the husband the right to retain the dowry as compensation. It highlights the Shia juristic view that such a declaration serves as a valid basis for the husband to accept the separation without the obligation of returning the *mahr*, distinguishing it from cases where the wife is at fault for specific misconduct.
